A duplicate identity path into the output node adds little.
Parallel convs into node 3 are redundant, so the direct conv adds less when a sibling conv exists.
A sibling conv at the merge node already provides conv capacity, so the second conv gains less.
With the sibling removed, edge 5 becomes the main deep path to the output.
With edge 1 removed, edge 5 only carries the weaker route through edges 0 and 2, so its gain shrinks.
Without the 0->2 branch, the 0->1->3 path carries more of the representation, so its conv matters more.
Another conv path already exists, so a conv on the parallel 0->2 route is partly redundant.
Without edge 1, node 2 receives only the weaker 0->1->2 route, so a conv on edge 5 gains less.
The 1x1->3x3 upgrade is incremental compared with upgrades from non-conv ops.
